newsitem.title: CANADA: St. Lawrence Seaway 1996 season ends.
newsitem.headline: St. Lawrence Seaway 1996 season ends.

text.p: The St. Lawrence Seaway closed Friday as the Emerald Star cleared the St. Lambert Locks near Montreal at 0711 EST/1211 GMT, the Seaway Authority said.
"The Seaway closed this morning. The last ship cleared," Authority spokeswoman Sylvie Moncion told Reuters.

Estimated cargo tonnage through the Welland Canal and the Montreal-Lake Ontario sections this year was about 49 million tonnes, about 2.5 percent higher than in 1995, a Seaway Authority statement said.
Steel slabs and steel product shipments were up 25 percent, it said. Iron ore and coal shipments rose 12 percent, and other bulk cargo was up two percent compared to the previous year.
Grain shipments declined due to "the lingering effects of ice on the Great Lakes and depleted grain stocks at the beginning of the season," the statement said.
Canada's eight-lock Welland Canal opened the 1996 season on March 29. The season saw 3,835 vessels transit the system.
In 1995 the shipping season closed December 28, after a ship that ran aground near the St. Lambert Locks was set afloat.
